newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine army turns down liquor ban suggestion.
newsitem.headline: Philippine army turns down liquor ban suggestion.

text.p: The chief of the Philippine armed forces commissary has rejected a call by a senator who wants to stop the sale of tax-free liquor to soldiers because he says it encourages drinking in military camps.
Commissary chief Navy Captain Rafaelito Sacdalan said on Tuesday most soldiers were assigned to remote posts away from their families and drinking was their only way of "unwinding."
The commissary also provided financial help to lowly-paid soldiers, he said.

Senate President Ernesto Maceda, in questioning the military policy, said violent incidents which occurred at military camps usually involved drunken soldiers. Incidents included soldiers firing into the air or shooting each other during quarrels.
"We are a democratic country. Soldiers can also drink for as long as they know how to drink," Sacdalan said.
